judged_text: deleteEvent replaces the working externalCalendarId || destinationCalendar.externalId fallback with the same dead find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) expression, so the resolved calendarId is undefined whenever externalCalendarId is absent. Cancelling any Google booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId (bookings created via the no-credentialId destination branch) calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId: undefined, the deletion rejects on the missing required parameter, and the event stays on the host's calendar after the app reports the booking cancelled — leaving attendee PII in a calendar event the user believes was removed.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` replace the prior fallback (`externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) with `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is absent/undefined (or null), this `find` predicate can never match a real calendar externalId, so the resolved calendar id becomes `undefined` instead of falling back to a destination calendar. This is a real behavioral regression for deletions/updates where the reference lacks `externalCalendarId` (or where the event lives on a non-primary calendar): the service will either call the Google API with an undefined/incorrect `calendarId`, or fall back to the wrong calendar later (if any fallback exists), leaving the event undeleted.
